metadata.reproducibility_rate: 91% of nixpkgs builds are bit-for-bit reproducible

core_concepts.definition: Packages built from pure functions where identical inputs produce identical /nix/store paths
core_concepts.hash_algorithm: SHA-256 truncated to 160 bits → base32 encoding (32 characters)
core_concepts.critical_property: Changing ANY input (including whitespace in builder scripts) changes store path

core_concepts.definition: Store path hash computed over derivation inputs (ATerm serialization)
inputs_included: ALL transitive dependency store paths (recursive hashing)
core_concepts.security_property: Input integrity required; compromised compiler produces different outputs with same hash

core_concepts.definition: Store path hash computed over ACTUAL OUTPUT CONTENT (not derivation inputs)
core_concepts.security_property: Output verified before substitution; immune to compromised build tools
core_concepts.limitation: Only works for pure content fetches; cannot include build steps

core_concepts.definition: Store path hash computed over output content + derivation inputs
core_concepts.limitation: Fails for 9% of nixpkgs (non-reproducible packages like chromium, rustc)

evaluation_phase.description: Nix language expressions parsed into derivation objects (ATerms)
evaluation_phase.security_boundary: Critical vulnerability surface - malicious flakes execute arbitrary code during nix flake show

build_phase.environment: Linux namespaces (mount, network, PID, user, time frozen to epoch 1)
build_phase.security_boundary: Strong isolation on Linux; weak on macOS (no user namespaces)

root_types: Temporary roots (/run/nix/gcroots/* - tmpfs, lost on reboot)
core_concepts.reference_tracking: ELF DT_NEEDED + RPATH scanning, script shebangs, archive recursion
core_concepts.critical_command: nix-store -q --referrers-closure /nix/store/... shows WHY path is alive

language_syntax.anti_pattern: with pkgs; [...] - breaks reproducibility, causes name collisions, rejected by nixpkgs maintainers
language_syntax.evaluation_semantics: LAZY - values computed only when accessed; order irrelevant
language_syntax.lookup_complexity: O(log n) via sorted vector (not hash map)

language_syntax.quadratic_pitfall: Repeated concatenation in loop: bad = n: if n==0 then [] else bad(n-1)++[n] → O(n²)
language_syntax.lazy_evaluation: Elements evaluated ONLY when accessed via builtins.elemAt
language_syntax.infinite_lists: Possible via recursion: let ones = 1 : ones; in builtins.elemAt ones 1000000

language_syntax.indented: ''multi-line'' - NO escaping, ''${ for literal ${, strips common leading indent
language_syntax.critical_footgun: String concatenation loses path properties: "/nix/store/" + hash → plain string (NO reference tracking)

language_syntax.attrset_pattern: { a, b ? 10, ... }: a + b - multi-param via destructuring
language_syntax.default_args: Evaluated LAZILY - only computed if accessed
language_syntax.at_pattern: args@{ a, b }: { sum = a+b; original = args } binds entire attrset

language_syntax.syntax: let a = 1; b = a + 1; in b * 2
language_syntax.shadowing: Inner bindings shadow outer bindings lexically
language_syntax.recursion: Direct and mutual recursion allowed; limited by ~10,000 frame stack depth
language_syntax.forward_reference: Illegal in attrsets without rec: { a = b + 1; b = 2; } → error

language_syntax.mechanism: Path interpolation adds context: s = "${pkgs.bash}/bin" carries reference to pkgs.bash
language_syntax.propagation: Context preserved through string operations: s2 = s + " --version" still has context
language_syntax.stripping: builtins.toString s removes context → plain string
language_syntax.security_risk: Context leakage into derivation names exposes secrets: pname = "app-${secret}" → store path contains secret

commands.typical_use: Quick CLI tool access: nix shell nixpkgs#ripgrep -c rg --version

commands.best_practice: Only run on trusted flakes; pin inputs first via nix flake lock

Show paths that reference given store path
commands.gc_debugging: Critical for understanding why path cannot be garbage collected

Verify flake builds successfully across all declared systems

microservice_patterns.deployment: nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#<hostname> for atomic upgrades with rollback

microservice_patterns.networking: Containers share host network namespace by default; use systemd.nspawn.networking = false for isolation
microservice_patterns.storage: bindMounts for persistent state: { source = "/var/lib/host-data"; target = "/data"; }
microservice_patterns.advantage: No Docker daemon required; containers built from Nix derivations

implementation.reproducibility: created = "1970-01-01T00:00:01Z" fixes timestamp for bit-for-bit reproducibility
implementation.oci_compliance: NixOS 25.11 dockerTools produces OCI-compliant images by default

microservice_patterns.deployment: docker load < result or skopeo copy docker-archive:result docker://registry/image:tag

security_boundaries.threat_model: Nix expressions evaluated directly on host machine with full filesystem/network access
security_boundaries.attack_vector: Malicious flake executes arbitrary code during nix flake show
mitigations: Never evaluate untrusted flakes without auditing
Pin all inputs via nix flake lock before evaluation
Air-gapped environments: disable network during eval (--option http-connections 0)

isolation_mechanisms: Mount namespaces: /nix/store read-only except output path
Network namespaces: loopback only (no external network)
User namespaces: builds as unprivileged nixbld user (UID 30000+)
Time namespace: frozen to UNIX epoch 1
limitations: macOS: NO user namespaces → sandboxing fundamentally weaker (sandbox-exec only)
Windows/WSL2: sandboxing via Windows containers (less mature)
Kernel vulnerabilities can break namespace isolation (CVE history)
security_boundaries.verification: nix show-config | grep sandbox → should be true

security_boundaries.allowed_users_privileges: Build packages but NOT bypass security controls
security_boundaries.critical_rule: trusted-users should NEVER include unprivileged users - equivalent to root access

security_boundaries.attack_vector: Cache poisoning - compromised cache serves malicious NAR with valid signature
security_boundaries.mitigation: Pin trusted-public-keys to exact fingerprints; never use wildcards

cross_compilation.libc_problem: Target binaries link against TARGET libc; build tools run on HOST libc

cross_compilation.rust_buildrs: Compiles for HOST but generates code for TARGET → cargoBuildFlags = "--target ${targetSystem}"
cross_compilation.python_cext: Must compile against target Python + target libc → python.pkgsCross.${targetSystem}.buildPythonPackage
cross_compilation.failure_rate: FFI boundaries cause 80% of cross-compilation failures

cross_compilation.purpose: Execute ARM64 binary on x86_64 host for testing
cross_compilation.limitation: Performance overhead; cannot test kernel interactions

module_system.priority_1: mkForce - ignores all lower priorities (emergency override only)
module_system.priority_4: mkDefault - only used if no higher priority value exists
module_system.determinism: Import order DOES NOT matter - priority system ensures deterministic resolution

module_system.simple_types: Last definition wins (unless overridden by priority)
module_system.submodule: Merges nested option definitions according to their types

reproducibility_limits.manifestation: Embedded in ELF binaries (build-id), ZIP archives
Affects JIT compilers (V8, JVM) → non-deterministic code generation
GCC parallel LTO, Rust incremental compilation
find/glob without sorting → directory entry order varies by FS/kernel

reproducibility_limits.current_rate: 91% of nixpkgs packages reproducible as of February 2026
reproducibility_limits.non_reproducible: chromium, electron, rustc, ghc (complex build systems, JIT compilers)

platform_specific.sandboxing_limitation: No user namespaces → sandboxing fundamentally weaker (sandbox-exec only)
platform_specific.filesystem_issue: Default APFS case-insensitive → breaks packages assuming case-sensitive FS
platform_specific.notarization: GUI apps require Apple notarization; Gatekeeper blocks unsigned Nix store paths
platform_specific.sip_impact: System Integrity Protection prevents modifying /usr/bin → requires PATH manipulation

platform_specific.filesystem_performance: /mnt/c extremely slow for I/O-heavy builds → MUST store Nix store in WSL2 ext4 (/home/user/.local/share/nix)
platform_specific.case_sensitivity: NTFS case-preserving but case-insensitive → breaks Linux packages
platform_specific.mitigation: fsutil file SetCaseSensitiveInfo on per-directory basis
platform_specific.symlink_limitation: Requires Windows Developer Mode for symlinks
platform_specific.daemon_support: No multi-user daemon support → single-user mode only

platform_specific.native_builds: aarch64-darwin packages build at native speed
platform_specific.cross_compilation: x86_64-linux → aarch64-linux works well; macOS cross-compilation limited

nixos_specific.purpose: Prevents automatic migration of stateful data between NixOS versions
nixos_specific.critical_rule: MUST match nixpkgs channel version (e.g., "25.11" for nixos-25.11)
nixos_specific.breakage_scenario: Upgrading nixpkgs without updating stateVersion → database format mismatches

nixos_specific.purpose: Pre-configured modules for specific hardware (Framework laptops, Raspberry Pi, etc.)
nixos_specific.benefit: Optimal kernel parameters, firmware, and driver configuration for specific devices

nixos_specific.purpose: Hydra-based CI for nixpkgs pull requests
nixos_specific.mass_rebuild_threshold: >200 package rebuilds requires staging branch (weekly merge window)
nixos_specific.direct_merge_threshold: <50 rebuilds can merge directly to master
nixos_specific.validation: All direct rebuilds must succeed; binary cache hits required for critical packages

nixos_specific.generation: Automatically generated from NixOS module system
nixos_specific.purpose: Idempotent system configuration (users, groups, systemd units, sysctl)
nixos_specific.rollback_mechanism: nixos-rebuild switch --rollback executes previous generation's activate script

performance_pitfalls.bad_pattern: bad = n: if n==0 then [] else bad(n-1)++[n] → O(n²)
performance_pitfalls.good_pattern: Accumulate in reverse with single final reverse: go i acc = if i>n then reverse acc else go(i+1)(acc++[i])
performance_pitfalls.complexity: O(n) vs O(n²) - 10,000 elements: milliseconds vs seconds

performance_pitfalls.scenario: Large folds without forcing intermediate results → OOM
performance_pitfalls.bad_pattern: sum = lst: foldl' (acc: x: acc+x) 0 lst on 1M elements
performance_pitfalls.fix: Force intermediate: foldl' (acc: x: seq (acc+x) (acc+x)) 0 lst
performance_pitfalls.mechanism: builtins.seq evaluates first argument, returns second

performance_pitfalls.limit: Stack depth limit ~10,000 frames applies to attrset nesting depth
performance_pitfalls.error: let nest = n: if n==0 then {} else { child = nest(n-1) }; in nest 10001 → stack overflow
performance_pitfalls.workaround: Flatten structure or use iterative algorithms

performance_pitfalls.bad_pattern: bad = n: if n==0 then "" else bad(n-1)+"x" → O(n²)
